title: Copying another child's play is listed at 15 months
summary: Most children copy other children while playing by about 15 months, CDC says.
body: CDC's example is taking toys out when another child does. The item sits on the 15-month social list, and most means 75 percent or more. Copying a peer during play is imitation in company, not the later milestone of joining a group game. The materials are not a diagnosis and not a validated screen. A lab study of copying chores is a different page and a different act.
